pr_body:
Add W3CLogger which writes server logs in the format described here: https://www.loganalyzer.net/log-analyzer/w3c-extended.html, and here: https://www.w3.org/TR/WD-logfile.html. Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/31843.

Questions/TODOs called out in comments below. Additional TODOs:

- [x] write more tests (in progress)
- [x] implement `cs-uri-stem`: "the value of the cs-uri-stem field is equal to the URL actually used by the client, truncated at the first "?" character." Might need to get this from routing info, since it's the URI that actually gets resolved, not necessarily the one that the client requested. Full spec here: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-wmlog/fc4b49d7-e83f-4389-8063-414f8bad80dd. @JamesNK any ideas on the best way to get this one? 
- [x] Logger should roll files when max_file_size is reached
- [x] Update when Options update
pr_comments: Has there been any thoughts on not having a public logger that you need to setup and instead having it be directly part of HttpLogging? Looks like it already has an indirect reliance on HttpLogging

> Has there been any thoughts on not having a public logger that you need to setup and instead having it be directly part of HttpLogging? Looks like it already has an indirect reliance on HttpLogging

I hadn't considered that yet, but it seems reasonable. I'd essentially just move everything from `Logging.W3C` to `HttpMiddleware` and have the `Logging.W3C` stuff not be public. I could probably consolidate the two `Fields` types that way as well

> implement `cs-uri-stem`: "the value of the cs-uri-stem field is equal to the URL actually used by the client, truncated at the first "?" character." Might need to get this from routing info, since it's the URI that actually gets resolved, not necessarily the one that the client requested. Full spec here: [docs.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-wmlog/fc4b49d7-e83f-4389-8063-414f8bad80dd](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-wmlog/fc4b49d7-e83f-4389-8063-414f8bad80dd). @JamesNK any ideas on the best way to get this one?

Routing just uses `HttpContext.Request.Path`.

> Routing just uses HttpContext.Request.Path.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/33251/commits/418e11c5f0317483a671e5eeaefef2e298fee278
Should we move the rolling file log component into its own class?

> Should we move the rolling file log component into its own class?

Right now I'm doing it in `W3CLoggerProcessor`. I could move the part that does the message processing/rolling/file-writing into another class & have `W3CLoggerProcessor` extend that, with the addition of the W3C-specific stuff (directives)

FWIW, for file rolling, I'm going with the same approach as https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Logging.AzureAppServices/src/FileLoggerProvider.cs, but modified to roll to a new file when `max_length` is reached - group messages by date, write to date-specific files until `max_length` is reached, then move to a new file. Delete oldest file when `max_retained_files` is reached

This is updated to include file rolling now. I created `FileLoggerProcessor` which does the work of a rolling file logger & had `W3CLoggerProcessor` extend it to write the W3C directives. I also added `FileLoggerOptions` which `W3CLoggerOptions` extends. Also applied some feedback. Need to add tests still for `FileLoggerProcessor` (specifically for rolling), and respond to a couple outstanding feedback items, but this should be ready for final-ish review.

Tests are failing on Helix at `Assert.True(File.Exists(fileName));` - @MattGal @HaoK these tests are testing the File Logger I added in this PR, which, in the tests, is writing to `Path.GetTempFileName()`. Would that behavior be different on Helix?

issue_context.title: Add W3C logging to HttpLogging middleware
issue_context.body:
We want to extend the HttpLogging Middleware to include W3C logs. 

Hazy details:

- Logging Provider
- Logging inside of the middleware to a different logger
- Making sure format is consistent (no extra fields per request/response)

@shirhatti can you help with specific details here?
comments:
The spec - https://www.w3.org/TR/WD-logfile.html

The fields IIS could log are at https://www.loganalyzer.net/log-analyzer/w3c-extended.html. You don't have to include all of them (win32status for example)

review_comments: nit: Helper method for building the path. Reduce duplication.
Double dispose if the following `TryCreateDirectory` returns false
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/33251/commits/83050fd92fcf06353a109f83f27e0ce1430bc5d5
Why is this necessary? Isn't this only called once per StreamWriter already?

Because FileLoggerProcessor calls `OnFirstWrite` when its file is empty or nonexistant - in the case of tests, the file is always empty or nonexistant, so without this every line would be preceded by the fields directive/headers

Since we know the only consumer of this data is StreamWriter, can you delay the Format, enqueue the elements array, and format when writing to the stream? This intermediate string is likely large and useless.

It's OK if you make a list of perf specific work in a follow-up issue.
Good idea - I'll file a follow-up issue for this one

This is only used when there are no pending logs, so isn't the meaning different?
The way I read this is "every period (1 second) we will flush any logs that were written within the last second". But the behavior is "we will flush logs with a maximum delay of the given period (1 second)"
Fair enough
This should probably be a thread
LongRunning?

Actually, it doesn't seem to matter since ProcessLogQueue uses async/await, it will keep spawning tasks.
http://blog.i3arnon.com/2015/07/02/task-run-long-running/

I used Task since I got it from BatchingLoggerProvider: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/44bcd96cc93131bdcf184bd7e22364c7dab18a96/src/Logging.AzureAppServices/src/BatchingLoggerProvider.cs#L159

Though ConsoleLoggerProcessor uses a Thread: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/207bb77acbbb9d21c1c3e4a106899debee1aaccb/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Console/src/ConsoleLoggerProcessor.cs#L25-L30. What would be the benefit of switching?
I don't think there's a benefit since this is async.
Just throwing an idea. There could be an `IStartupfilter` which adds the middleware at the first of the pipeline so there's no need to call `app.UseW3cLogging`.
Why would we do that for this middleware?
Should W3CLoggerProcessor be resolved from DI? It seems to be the one that has DI dependencies, and that you're needing to do this virtual override to test.
Yeah, seems like it could. I'll include that as a follow-up item.
Adding warning this can contain PII/auth information and should only be used when logs are secure and ACLed

"Cookie contents can contain authentication tokens, or private information which may have regulatory concerns under GDPR and other laws. Cookies should not be logged unless logs are secure and access controlled and the privacy impact accessed."
Figure out how to make this sealed
Should we be checking if this is an absolute path?
More content that should be written directly to the streamWriter.
nit: stackalloc
I don't think you can stackalloc arrays of reference types. Also, this array is still referenced after the method exits.

>I don't think you can stackalloc arrays of reference types.

Doh, Array pool then 😄 

>Also, this array is still referenced after the method exits.

It isn't, gets converted into a string then pushed to the logger. Although looks like there was some discussion about changing a bunch of the formatting to do it later, so maybe this should wait.
Why did you change this? It's now a hot loop when there are no pending logs

Ok reading more, this is to support the file rolling stuff, but I think it should be done differently. Process logs as they come in, you're going to get the logs from Day 1 next to each other, and logs from Day 2 after all Day 1 logs, so no need for most of this logic to group logs etc.
Should there be a limit to how many messages you batch at a time? Under load you could get stuck in this loop and _currentBatch could grow indefinitely.
Why are these types separate? FileLoggerProcessor isn't used anywhere else.
To make it easier to extend this to a general purpose file logger in the future
@blowdart could you have a look at the fields being logged by default?
If that is just lines 112-114 then that's fine. But the comment at 109 says it includes request headers, and I don't see inclusions/exclusions for that anywhere.
I fixed up the request/request headers options to not include cookie
Is this in UTC time? Should we be using DateTime.UtcNow below? (DateTime.UtcNow is faster than DateTime.Now)
No, it'll be in local time
Why 10 MiB?

When storing the `_loggingFields` as a field, it won't update when `IOptionsMonitor<W3CLoggerOptions>` detect changes.
